belief: God’s will is always the thing I least want.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that God’s will is always the thing you least want, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Fear that God will send you somewhere you dread if you surrender to Him. Teaching that emphasized sacrifice without joy. A parent who withheld good things. Assuming that if you want something, it must be selfish. Picturing God as a stern boss rather than a loving Father.
teaches: God’s will sometimes involves hard things, and following Jesus includes sacrifice. But God is not looking for ways to make you miserable. Jesus said that if earthly parents give good gifts, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask. God’s will is good, pleasing, and perfect. As you delight in the LORD, He shapes your desires and gives you the desires of your heart. His plans for His people include hope and a future.
self_statements: If I want it, God probably doesn’t.
God will make me do what I hate.
Surrendering to God means losing everything I love.
God’s plan is always the hardest path.
My desires don’t matter to God.
God likes to make me uncomfortable.
errors: Picturing God as a stern or withholding authority figure.
Turning “God’s will is sometimes hard” into “it’s always what I least want.”
Overlooking God’s goodness and the joy of following Him.
Avoiding surrender because you fear God’s plans.
questions: Would a loving father give his child a stone instead of bread?
How does Romans 12:2 describe God’s will?
What happens to my desires as I delight in the LORD?
Has God ever given me something good that I wanted?
Am I picturing God like someone from my past?
Is it possible God put some of my desires in me?
What would it look like to trust God’s goodness with my plans?
truth: God’s will is not always the thing I least want. My Father in heaven gives good gifts. His will is good, pleasing, and perfect. Sometimes it includes hard things, but always for my good. As I delight in Him, He shapes my desires and gives me the desires of my heart.
hw_questions: Would a loving father give a stone for bread?
What happens to my desires as I delight in God?
Has God given me good things I wanted?
Am I picturing God like someone from my past?
Did God put some desires in me?
hw_truths: God’s will is good, pleasing, and perfect.
As I delight in God, He shapes my desires.
God’s plans for me include hope.
Hard things in God’s will are for my good.
In God’s presence there is joy.
log: Each day, write one good gift God gave me that I wanted or enjoyed.
name_example: Sarah can delight herself in the LORD, and He will give her the desires of her heart.
actions: Write a list of good things God has given you
Tell God honestly what you want,
and ask Him to shape your desires.
and write what it says about your Father’s heart.
about a time God’s will turned out better than they expected.
prayer: Father, thank You that You give good gifts to Your children. Help me reject the lie that Your will is always the thing I least want. Teach me to delight in You, to trust Your goodness, and to believe that Your will is good, pleasing, and perfect. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
